msg: No commitment sentence. The EU model statement opens by naming the body and stating it is committed to making the site accessible.
No legal basis cited. Name Directive (EU) 2016/2102 (or its national transposition), or Directive (EU) 2019/882 for a private-sector service.
The statement never says which website, app or service it covers. One statement per covered site is the model's unit.
No compliance status. The model allows exactly three wordings: fully compliant, partially compliant, or not compliant.
Two different compliance statuses appear in one statement. A monitoring body reads the status as a single declared value.
EN 301 549 is not named. The status has to be measured against the harmonised standard, not against WCAG alone.
An EN 301 549 version older than V3.2.1 is cited. V3.2.1 is the version listed in the Official Journal for the Web Accessibility Directive.
Status is partially or not compliant, but there is no Non-accessible content section. That section is what makes the status verifiable.
Non-accessible content is listed with no reason category. The model has exactly three: non-compliance, disproportionate burden, and content outside the scope of the legislation.
Disproportionate burden is claimed with no assessment behind it. Article 5 of Directive (EU) 2016/2102 allows the claim only after an assessment of the burden.
Disproportionate burden is claimed with no accessible alternative offered for the excluded content.

label: prepar(ed|ation)
msg: No date of preparation. The model requires the date the statement was prepared or last fully revised.

label: prepar(ed|ation)
msg: The date of preparation is in the future, so the statement cannot have been prepared yet.
The preparation method is missing. Say whether this was a self-assessment or an evaluation by a third party.

label: last review(ed)?|reviewed on
msg: No date of last review. The statement has to carry the date it was last checked, separate from the date it was written.

label: last review(ed)?|reviewed on
msg: The last review is more than 12 months old. Directive (EU) 2016/2102 Article 7(1) requires the statement to be kept up to date, and monitoring bodies sample by date.
No feedback mechanism. A reader must be able to report an accessibility barrier and request content in an accessible form.
No enforcement procedure. The statement must point to the body a reader can escalate to when the feedback goes unanswered.
A template placeholder was never filled in. This is the most common defect in generated statements and it is visible to the public.
